current_p1_ru: Блондинка в законе, Дьявол носит Prada, Деловая девушка, С девяти до пяти. Ты любишь, когда сильная героиня показана с улыбкой. Не «героический подвиг»; просто умная девочка, которая делает дело и при этом весело.
current_p1_en:
Legally Blonde, The Devil Wears Prada, Working Girl, Nine to Five. You love when a strong heroine is shown with a smile. Not "a heroic feat"; just a smart girl who does the work and has fun doing it.
Why it lands: you understand: propaganda through seriousness works worse than propaganda through lightness. Many more people will see feminism through Elle Woods than through heavy drama.
People sometimes devalue it: "that's just pop." Pop that changed more minds than a manifesto.
What's worth knowing: "light" feminism works in combination with serious. If you watch only the light, you risk thinking everything's already solved. The serious films remind you of the price of these victories. Both registers — together.

current_p1_ru: Контакт, Безумный Макс, Чудо-женщина, Силквуд. Тебя цепляют истории, где женщина одна против мира. Не «команда» — а одиночный путь, в котором либо выиграешь, либо погибнешь.
current_p1_en:
Contact, Mad Max, Wonder Woman, Silkwood. What grabs you are stories where a woman is alone against the world. Not "a team" — but a solo path where you either win or perish.
The logic is simple: you have an interest in solo heroism. Most films now are about teams; you love when the focus is on one figure.
People are sometimes surprised: "but a team is stronger." In cinema — yes. In reality often not. Great women often went alone, and that's an interesting archetype.
What's worth knowing: "the loner" as ideal is sometimes a refusal of help. In reality even the strongest women rely on networks — friends, mentors, allies. Learn to value solo cinema and collaborative life. The screen heroine carries everything herself. You don't have to.

current_p1_ru: Перспективная девушка, Тельма и Луиза, Силквуд, Безумный Макс. Тебе ближе фильмы, в которых женская сила — не светлая. Это месть, гнев, борьба до последнего, иногда с трагическим финалом.
current_p1_en:
Promising Young Woman, Thelma & Louise, Silkwood, Mad Max. You're closer to films where female power is not bright. It's revenge, anger, fight to the last, sometimes with a tragic finale.
It works because you have a mature attitude toward justice. Not "everything will end well"; sometimes you have to win at a high cost, and cinema is honest about it.
People sometimes can't take it: "why such a dark ending?." Because sometimes life is like that. And lying in cinema isn't respect for the viewer.
What's worth knowing: dark justice is wonderful, but sometimes becomes a fetish. If you love only the dark, you stop seeing victories that come without bloodshed. Learn to value brighter stories too. Real change often happens quietly, not dramatically.

current_p1_ru: Кофе, прогулка, ужин в ресторане, книжный магазин. Тебе нужен классический формат свидания. Не «креативно»; а проверенно — там, где можно говорить и быть собой.
current_p1_en:
Coffee, walk, dinner at a restaurant, bookstore. You need a classical date format. Not "creative"; but proven — where you can talk and be yourself.
Why it lands: you know what dating is for. "Impressing" isn't enough for you; you need to really get to know the person.
People sometimes say: "coffee is banal." Banal. And ideal for a first meeting.
What's worth knowing: classical formats work if you yourself aren't banal. Coffee with an interesting person is interesting; with a boring one — boring. The place doesn't make the date.

current_p1_ru: Спорт вместе, поездка за город, пикник в парке, выставка. Тебе нужно совместное действие. Не «сидеть и говорить»; а делать что-то и через это узнавать друг друга.
current_p1_en:
Activity together, a trip out of town, picnic in the park, exhibition. You need joint action. Not "sit and talk"; but do something and through this get to know each other.
The logic is simple: you have a kinesthetic approach. It's hard for you to "just talk"; you need action as background.
People are sometimes surprised: "bowling on a date right away?." Right away. You see how a person loses — that's the best test of character.
What's worth knowing: active dates sometimes put a partner in an awkward position. If they don't like sport, your choice can seem like pressure. Learn to feel. Before suggesting, find out preferences.

current_p1_ru: Кино, выставка, концерт, книжный магазин. Тебе нужно общее культурное переживание. Не «обсудить погоду»; а получить вместе впечатление и потом его обсудить.
current_p1_en:
Cinema, exhibition, concert, bookstore. You need a shared cultural experience. Not "discuss the weather"; but get an impression together and then discuss it.
It works because you have cultural depth. "A date for the sake of a date" isn't enough for you; you need the evening itself to be valuable.
People sometimes say: "you don't talk in a museum." Not during — but afterwards. And those are often the best conversations.
What's worth knowing: cultural dates work with those who share your level of interest. If a person goes to the museum "because you wanted", they're bored, and it's visible. Learn to feel. Not everyone is your person.

current_p1_ru: Ночной город, крыша, бар, ужин в ресторане. Тебе нужна атмосфера. Не «дневной кофе»; а что-то с настроением — огни, ветер, темнота.
current_p1_en:
Night city, rooftop, bar, dinner at a restaurant. You need atmosphere. Not daytime coffee, but something with mood — lights, wind, darkness.
It works because you're aesthetically sensitive. It matters to you not only "with whom", but also "where."
People sometimes get snobby: "you're a romantic." A romantic. And I don't apologize for it.
What's worth knowing: "atmospheric" places are often more expensive. Learn to plan the budget. And not every partner will appreciate it — for some, a warm café matters more than a fashionable rooftop.

current_p1_ru: Готовить вместе дома, кино дома, кофе, прогулка. Ты любишь свидания не «выйти», а «остаться вместе». Дом для тебя — это интимная территория, и пускать туда — серьёзный шаг.
current_p1_en:
Cooking together at home, movie at home, coffee, walk. You love dates that aren't "go out", but "stay together." Home for you is intimate territory, and letting in is a serious step.
It works because you have a deep relationship with intimacy. Not many dates with random people, but a serious connection with one person.
People are sometimes surprised: "cooking on a first date?." Not on a first. But soon after.
What's worth knowing: home dates work when there's trust. If you invite home too quickly, the partner can read it as pressure. Learn to feel the tempo.

current_p1_ru: Спонтанно куда глаза глядят, поездка за город, прогулка, пикник. Тебе нужна непредсказуемость. Не «расписанный план»; а возможность оказаться где-то неожиданном.
current_p1_en:
Spontaneously wherever, a trip out of town, walk, picnic. You need unpredictability. Not "a scheduled plan"; but the chance to end up somewhere unexpected.
Why it lands: you have a love for the moment. The best dates happen when you don't know what will happen.
People sometimes worry: "what if nothing works out?." It'll work out. With me, something always works out.
What's worth knowing: spontaneity works with someone who shares it. If the partner is a planner, your "spontaneity" is their horror. Learn to adapt. Sometimes worth preparing a plan B, and spontaneity will work only when both are ready.

current_p1_ru: Кофе, прогулка, книжный магазин, спорт. Тебе важен первый формат. Что-то лёгкое, без давления, где можно встретиться, поговорить, и без обязательств — увидеть, есть ли искра.
current_p1_en:
Coffee, walk, bookstore, sport. The first format matters to you. Something light, without pressure, where you can meet, talk, and without obligations — see if there's a spark.
The logic is simple: you have the wisdom of trial dates. Not "dinner for 3 hours right away"; but a 30-60 minute test.
People sometimes say: "you're somehow superficial." Not superficial — wise. After 30 minutes it's already clear whether to continue.
What's worth knowing: "short first dates" are also a risk. Sometimes people open up at the second hour. Learn to feel. If there's at least some interest after 30 minutes, extend. Maybe the main thing is just beginning.

current_p1_ru: Драма, исторический, военный, документальный. Ты не «развлекаешься» в кино; ты получаешь опыт. Тебе нужно, чтобы фильм оставил след — не «было прикольно», а «теперь думаю».
current_p1_en:
Drama, history, war, documentary. You don't go to cinema just to be entertained; you go for an experience. You need a film to leave a trace — not "that was fun," but "now I'm thinking.".
It works because you have a mature attitude toward art. Most people go to the cinema to distract themselves; you — to immerse.
People sometimes don't get it: "you're watching something heavy again?." Again. And I need it.
What's worth knowing: serious depth is wonderful, but it requires resource. If you're in a bad state, a heavy film can deepen it. Learn to alternate — not from lowering standards, but from caring for yourself. The film will still be there; your inner state needs to be ready for the encounter.

current_p1_ru: Боевик, триллер, криминал, военный. Тебе нужно, чтобы фильм гнал тебя. Ты не сидишь спокойно; ты вцепился(-ась) в кресло, ты дышишь учащённо, и это тебя заряжает.
current_p1_en:
Action, thriller, crime, war. You need a film to move fast. You don't sit calmly; you're clutching the chair, you're breathing fast, and that charges you.
Why it lands: you have a need for stress in game form. Real stress — bad; cinematic — a controlled dose, and it releases you.
People are sometimes surprised: "you're tensing up." Tensing up and enjoying it.
What's worth knowing: adrenaline cinema is great, but not the only kind. If you only watch this, your nervous system gets used to one register. Learn to alternate with the slow. Otherwise quiet films start to feel "empty", and you lose access to half of cinema. Both modes — together.

current_p1_ru: Детектив, мистика, научная фантастика, триллер. Тебе нужно, чтобы фильм заставлял разгадывать. Ты не просто смотришь; ты решаешь.
current_p1_en:
Detective, mystery, sci-fi, thriller. You need a film that makes you solve something. You don't just watch; you're working.
The logic is simple: you have an analytical mind. Most films feel too "direct" for you; you need a knot to untangle.
People sometimes get tired: "why are you rewatching it again?." I haven't understood it all yet.
What's worth knowing: intellectual films are wonderful, but sometimes become an end in themselves. The strongest ones are those where the solution carries emotion, not just satisfaction. Learn to value the films where you cried after the answer, not just nodded. Reason and feeling — best together.

current_p1_ru: Фэнтези, научная фантастика, приключения, мистика. Ты любишь, когда фильм уносит. Не современный мир, а другой — где другие правила, другие существа, другая физика.
current_p1_en:
Fantasy, sci-fi, adventure, mystery. You love when a film carries you away. Not the modern world, but another — with different rules, different beings, different physics.
It works because you have a strong imagination. The real world feels cramped to you; you need wider worlds.
People sometimes don't get it: "that's just escapism." Yes. So what? Escapism is a normal human need.
What's worth knowing: Fantastic worlds are beautiful, but sometimes become a refuge. If you're only in them, you lose connection with the present. Learn to alternate. Otherwise your mind becomes a tourist, not a resident. Other worlds — to visit. This world — to live in.

current_p1_ru: Комедия, романтическая комедия, приключения, фэнтези. Тебе нужно, чтобы фильм поднимал настроение. Не «учил жизни», не «ломал представление о реальности» — просто радовал.
current_p1_en:
Comedy, rom-com, adventure, fantasy. You need a film to lift your mood. Not "to teach you life", not "to shatter your view of reality" — just to please.
It works because you have a mature attitude toward your own emotions. You understand sometimes you need exactly lightness, and you don't feel embarrassed choosing comedy.
People sometimes get snobby: "you're not watching anything serious." Not always. But when I watch — pure joy.
What's worth knowing: light genres also have different depths. Not all comedies are equal. Learn to tell the witty from the flat. The best comedies are serious literature in disguise. Keep choosing lightness, but raise the bar — light doesn't have to mean dumb.

current_p1_ru: Хоррор, мистика, триллер, криминал. Ты не боишься страшного. Ты идёшь туда сознательно — потому что в страхе есть свой кайф, и в тёмных историях — свои откровения.
current_p1_en:
Horror, mystery, thriller, crime. You're not afraid of the scary. You go there consciously — because there's a thrill in fear, and revelations in dark stories.
Why it lands: you have a strong nervous system. Most people avoid the unpleasant; you can endure it and even love it.
People are sometimes surprised: "how do you watch this?." The same way you watch what bores me. Everyone has their own.
What's worth knowing: dark cinema is a dialogue with your own fears. If you're in a rough state right now, it can amplify them. Learn to feel when the dark is catharsis, and when it's submersion. The first heals; the second deepens. Reading your own state is part of the genre.

current_p1_ru: Исторический, вестерн, военный, драма. Тебе нравится, когда фильм — это эпос. Большие события, большие судьбы, большое полотно истории.
current_p1_en:
History, western, war, drama. You like when a film is an epic. Big events, big fates, big canvas of history.
The logic is simple: you have a sense of scale. Chamber stories about "I had problems at the office" bore you; you need something on a larger scale.
People are sometimes surprised: "you like the long ones?." Long. Epic requires time.
What's worth knowing: epic cinema is powerful, but requires patience. If you're in fast-dopamine mode, the epic won't land. Learn to set aside time. You watch the epic not "in between things", but as an event. Light a candle, turn off the phone, let the canvas open. That's the only way it works.

category_name: Герой кино, на которого ты похож
current_p1_ru: Форрест Гамп, Амели, Гермиона, Джо Марч. Тебя цепляют герои, которые не теряют веры в людей. Они могут быть наивными, но эта наивность — их сила, а не слабость.
current_p1_en:
Forrest Gump, Amelie, Hermione, Jo March. You're drawn to heroes who don't lose faith in people. They can be naive, but that naivete is their strength, not weakness.
It works because you have the ability to see the best in people. In a world where the cynical view is considered intelligent, you choose sincerity — and that's a rare maturity.
People are sometimes surprised: "are you like Forrest?." In some sense yes. And what's wrong with that?
What's worth knowing: trust is your strength, but sometimes becomes vulnerability. Learn to tell faith in people in general from faith in a specific person right now. The first — wonderful. The second — requires verification. Forrest is loved by the screenwriter; in real life, not everyone deserves your innocence.

category_name: Герой кино, на которого ты похож
current_p1_ru: Чувак (Big Lebowski), Уолтер Митти, Энди Дюфрейн. Ты герой, который не торопится. Жизнь идёт, а ты не суетишься. И в этой неторопливости куда больше мудрости, чем в гонке других.
current_p1_en:
The Dude (The Big Lebowski), Walter Mitty, Andy Dufresne. You're a hero who doesn't rush. Life goes on, and you don't fuss. And in that unhurried pace there's much more wisdom than in others' race.
Why it lands: you have your own tempo. In an era where everyone hurries to "succeed", you chose to live.
People sometimes call it "laziness." Not laziness — a chosen tempo.
What's worth knowing: "not rushing" is wonderful as long as it stays conscious. If you don't rush because you don't want to act at all — that's no longer philosophy, that's paralysis. The Dude in the film has a screenwriter who carries him through plot; you have only yourself. Slow with attention — yes. Slow with avoidance — careful.

category_name: Герой кино, на которого ты похож
current_p1_ru: Шерлок Холмс, Тони Старк, Гермиона, Энди Дюфрейн. Ты узнаёшь себя в гениях, которые слишком умны для обычной среды. Они не «задаются» — просто видят больше, и от этого им сложнее жить с обычными людьми.
current_p1_en:
Sherlock Holmes, Tony Stark, Hermione, Andy Dufresne. You recognize yourself in geniuses who are too perceptive for their ordinary environment. They're not "showing off" — they just see more, and because of that, it's harder for them to live with ordinary people.
The logic is simple: you have a sense of your own non-standardness. You're not "ordinary"; you understand that, and sometimes it's lonely.
People sometimes don't get it: "you're a genius?." Not a genius. Different. That's different.
What's worth knowing: "outsider genius" is a tempting archetype, but sometimes becomes an excuse for not wanting to fit in. Learn to tell real unusualness from a pose. The first — yes, hard, deserves respect. The second — laziness in a beautiful wrapper. Genuine difference shows in work, not in complaints about "ordinary people".

category_name: Герой кино, на которого ты похож
current_p1_ru: Индиана Джонс, Итан Хант, Лара Крофт, Тони Старк. Ты любишь героев, у которых не бывает скучных дней. Они вечно в движении, в риске, в открытиях.
current_p1_en:
Indiana Jones, Ethan Hunt, Lara Croft, Tony Stark. You love heroes who don't have boring days. They're forever in motion, in risk, in discoveries.
It works because you have a hunger for adventure too. Sitting in one place is torture; you need to move, learn, risk.
People sometimes get tired of your energy: "just relax." And I'm comfortable in motion.
What's worth knowing: adventure is great motivation, but sometimes becomes flight from yourself. If you're constantly in motion, you can fail to understand who you are. Learn to stop sometimes. Indiana Jones in the film doesn't have an inner life between adventures; you do, and it deserves attention. Run, yes. Run from yourself, no.

category_name: Герой кино, на которого ты похож
current_p1_ru: Тайлер Дёрден, Китнисс, Скарлетт О'Хара, Лара Крофт. Тебя цепляют герои, которые не подчиняются системе. Они либо ломают её, либо строят свою.
current_p1_en:
Tyler Durden, Katniss, Scarlett O'Hara, Lara Croft. You're drawn to heroes who don't submit to the system. They either break it or build their own.
It works because you yourself have a streak of protest. You're not the kind who accepts "as is" without questions.
People sometimes worry: "you're not Tyler though." Not Tyler. But there's something in him I understand.
What's worth knowing: rebels in cinema often lose. Learn to tell healthy resistance from self-destruction. Not every "no" to the world is strength; sometimes it's just anger in bad packaging. The screen rebel has a screenwriter polishing his lines; in life, the same gesture often comes off as a tantrum. Aim where it changes things, not where it just blows up.

category_name: Герой кино, на которого ты похож
current_p1_ru: Майкл Корлеоне, Шерлок Холмс, Энди Дюфрейн, Итан Хант. Ты как герой, который думает на три шага вперёд. Не реактивный — стратегический.
current_p1_en:
Michael Corleone, Sherlock Holmes, Andy Dufresne, Ethan Hunt. You're like a hero who thinks three steps ahead. Not reactive — strategic.
Why it lands: you have a strategy for everything. Most people live reactively; you — proactively.
People are sometimes surprised: "you calculated all of this?." Calculated. And usually it works.
What's worth knowing: strategy is wonderful as long as it stays flexible. If you hold the plan too rigidly, reality will outplay you. Learn to adapt. The best strategists are the ones who change the plan in real time. The screen strategist wins because the screenwriter is on his side; in life, even the best plan meets weather, traffic, other people's moods. Plan — yes. Worship the plan — no.

category_name: Герой кино, на которого ты похож
current_p1_ru: Джо Марч, Китнисс, Скарлетт О'Хара, Амели. Тебя цепляют героини с чёткой внутренней силой. Не «жертвы», не «милашки» — а женщины, которые сами идут.
current_p1_en:
Jo March, Katniss, Scarlett O'Hara, Amelie. You're grabbed by heroines with clear inner strength. Not "victims", not "sweethearts" — but women who walk on their own.
The logic is simple: you value agency. Heroines who "happen to things" bore you; you need ones who act.
People sometimes call this "too feminist." Not feminist — normal. A woman's strength is normal strength, not a separate category.
What's worth knowing: every "strong woman" in cinema is a simplification. Real strong women are often weaker than they appear, and that's also normal. Learn to value more complex images too — the ones where strength coexists with doubt, fatigue, grief. Strength without cracks is a poster; strength through cracks is a person.

current_p1_ru: Молча лайкаешь, читаешь чужие споры, пишешь и удаляешь, ставишь сердечко. Ты в комментариях есть, но не виден. Читаешь всё, реагируешь молча.
current_p1_en:
You like silently, read other people's arguments, type and delete, drop a heart. You're present in the comments but not visible. You read everything, react silently.
It works because you have a healthy distance. Most climb into every argument; you know internet comments rarely become productive dialogue.
People sometimes don't even guess you're here at all. And that's your strategy — to be present without leaving a trace.
What's worth knowing: silent audience is critically important for content. If everyone is silent, authors feel they're not seen. Learn to at least occasionally drop a like — that's support without getting pulled in. A small gesture from your side can be the difference between an author burning out and continuing.

current_p1_ru: Споришь, поправляешь факты, иронизируешь, пишешь простыни. Ты не можешь пройти мимо. Если кто-то неправ, ты должен(-на) ответить — даже в случайном чужом посте.
current_p1_en:
You argue, correct facts, ironize, write walls of text. You can't pass by. If someone is wrong, you must answer — even on a random stranger's post.
Why it lands: you have a civic sense. It matters to you that lies don't go unanswered.
People sometimes get tired: "you're arguing again." Again. Someone has to.
What's worth knowing: arguing in comments is rarely productive. Algorithms love conflict and promote it. The more you write, the more you feed what you fight. Learn to choose battles. Sometimes the best reaction is ignoring. Your energy is a finite resource — spend it where it can actually change something.

current_p1_ru: «База», мемы вместо ответа, ирония, один символ. Ты пишешь на современном языке. Не «здравствуйте, спасибо за пост»; а «база» и эмодзи 💀.
current_p1_en:
"Baza", memes instead of replies, irony, one symbol. You write in modern language. Not "hello, thanks for the post"; but "baza" and the 💀 emoji.
It works because you live in modern internet culture. Most people over 35 don't understand this language; you do.
People sometimes don't catch up: "what does baza mean?." Agreement. Briefly.
What's worth knowing: internet slang ages quickly. What's cool in 2024, in 2026 will look old. Learn to accept this. Don't cling to one slang — it'll go away on its own. The fluency stays; the specific words rotate.

current_p1_ru: Задаёшь вопросы, поправляешь факты, пишешь простыни, поддерживаешь. Ты используешь комментарии как способ узнать. Не критика, не похвала — а вопрос.
current_p1_en:
You ask questions, correct facts, write walls of text, support. You use comments as a way to find out. Not criticism, not praise — a question.
It works because you have curiosity. It's not enough for you to read a post; you need to understand the author, their motives, their context.
People are sometimes surprised: "you have a question under every post?." Not for every. But if I have a sincere question, I ask it.
What's worth knowing: sincere questions are a rare thing in comments. Most "questions" are disguised criticism. Learn to formulate so the author hears exactly the interest. That'll give you more answers than you'd expect. Real curiosity is felt — and it's rewarded.

current_p1_ru: Тегаешь друга, мемы вместо ответа, комплименты автору, «первый». Ты используешь комменты как социальный инструмент. Зовёшь друга, помечаешь, объединяешь людей.
current_p1_en:
You tag a friend, memes instead of replies, compliments to the author, "first." You use comments as a social tool. Calling a friend, marking, uniting people.
Why it lands: you have social thinking. It's not enough for you to just read a post; you need to share it with specific people.
People love you for this. From you come posts they'd like, and they appreciate this.
What's worth knowing: tagging too often = turning into spam. If you tag Masha under every third post, she'll stop reacting. Learn to dose. One precise tag a week works ten times stronger than ten random ones. Restraint makes the gesture sharper.

current_p1_ru: Один символ, молчаливый лайк, сердечко, пишешь и удаляешь. Ты в комментах сжат(-а) до минимума. 💀, 🔥, ??? — этого хватает.
current_p1_en:
One symbol, silent like, heart, you type and delete. In comments, you compress yourself to the minimum. 💀, 🔥, ??? — that's enough.
The logic is simple: you understand: an emoji can contain a whole comment. No need for five sentences; one reaction says it all.
People sometimes don't distinguish: "you only put an emoji?." Yep. That's a complete thought.
What's worth knowing: minimalism works with those who understand it. With the older generation, "💀" under their post is "are you mocking?." Learn to adapt. Minimalism isn't a universal language. Save it for those fluent in the same code.
